sources.citation: Piatkowski J, Karbowiak L, Depta F. A lightweight algorithm for synchronized multimodal data acquisition using temporal sample alignment. Scientific Reports 15, 22711 (2025).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Experimentally demonstrates that heterogeneous sensor fusion requires a shared time reference and temporal sample alignment. It addresses acquisition engineering, not the Run 118 ecological coherence bound.

sources.citation: Terasaki Hart DE, Bui TN, Di Maggio L, et al. Global phenology maps reveal the drivers and effects of seasonal asynchrony. Nature 645, 133-140 (2025).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Uses multiple time-series products and independent validation to map real phenological asynchrony. It supports the need to model timing while challenging any assumption that all asynchrony is measurement error.

sources.citation: Lang W, Zhang Y, Li X, et al. Phenological divergence between plants and animals under climate change. Nature Ecology & Evolution 9, 261-272 (2025).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Analyzes nearly half a million terrestrial phenology time series and finds unequal temporal shifts. It challenges the common-mode assumption outside a preregistered local signal family.

sources.citation: Leung B, Gonzalez A. Global monitoring for biodiversity: Uncertainty, risk, and power analyses to support trend change detection. Science Advances 10, eadj1448 (2024).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Shows that uncertainty can prevent detection of biodiversity trend changes even at large sample sizes. Supports treating monitoring adequacy as a quantitative gate; does not test timing coherence.

sources.citation: Schulte to Buhne H, Pettorelli N. Better together: Integrating and fusing multispectral and radar satellite imagery to inform biodiversity monitoring, ecological research and conservation science. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 9, 849-865 (2018).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Documents the value and methodological complexity of fusing complementary remote-sensing streams for biodiversity monitoring. It is contextual rather than evidence for the exact theorem.
